newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toan Chay ready to be Cambodia first premier-report.
newsitem.headline: Toan Chay ready to be Cambodia first premier-report.

text.p: A former ally of ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said in an interview published on Tuesday that he is ready to succeed him and work with powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
In the interview in Phnom Penh with the Yomiuri Shimbun, Toan Chay, governor of Cambodia's northwestern Siem Reap province, sharply criticised Ranariddh.

"The prince is fond of living abroad. I do not think he is capable of leading efforts to rebuild the nation," Toan Chay said. The governor quit Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party last month shortly before fighting broke out between the two prime ministers.
Toan Chay said all members of the FUNCINPEC party were now willing to cooperate with Hun Sen and the return of royalist Foreign Minister Ung Huot would add to Hun Sen's efforts to unite the country.

"(Foreign Minister) Ung Huot is a remarkable person and an old friend of mine. I am delighted he is back. The only person within the FUNCINPEC party rejecting cooperation with Hun Sen is Ranariddh himself," he said.
Ung Huot returned to Cambodia on Monday saying he wanted to work for democracy and pluralism.

"I am fully prepared to accept the premiership. The international community might not immediately accept me but I must do this. If I try hard enough, the international community will understand," Toan Chay said.

Toan Chay said the party must first hold a convention to choose him as a candidate to succeed Ranariddh as party leader. After that, parliament must formally approve him, a process which could take about a month, he said.

Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed a coalition government after a U.N.-run election in May 1993. Hun Sen has said he does not want the job of first prime minister and called on FUNCINPEC members to choose a new person for the post.
He denies he staged a coup against Ranariddh and says he acted after his co-premier negotiated illegally with the Khmer Rouge and illegally imported weapons.
Many FUNCINPEC members and sympathisers fled from the country in the aftermath of Ranariddh's ouster and the execution of Ho Sok, a FUNCINPEC secretary of state at the interior ministry.
